sections.title: Vague on purpose
sections.content: majd points at the future without saying exactly when — closer to English "later" or "at some point" than to a specific time word like holnap or jövő héten. Because it's already vague, majd doesn't need fog to do the future-pointing job: it pairs comfortably with plain present tense, and just as comfortably with fog + infinitive when you want to add a stronger sense of prediction or promise on top.

items.spanish: Majd segítek neked, most nincs időm.
items.english: I'll help you later, I don't have time right now.

items.spanish: Egyelőre nem tudom, mit fogok csinálni — majd kiderül.
items.english: For now I don't know what I'll do — it'll become clear eventually.

items.spanish: Mindenesetre majd írok, ha lesz egy szabad hónapom.
items.english: In any case I'll write when I have a free month.

sections.content: Majd kiderül ("it'll become clear", "we'll see") is a whole fixed phrase Hungarians reach for constantly — a perfect all-purpose reply when you genuinely don't want to commit to a plan yet.
